Ultraviolet Observation with Astrosat: Catalog of UV-bright sources, Globular Clusters and Galactic star counts

Abstract:

The Ultraviolet Imaging Telescope (UVIT) on board AstroSat, launched in 2015, is the first indigenous scientific mission of India. We have performed a statistical analysis of the UVIT observations over the last decade and prepared a catalogue of sources, and subsequently classified them. The catalogue consists of observations of various types of astrophysical objects, including open and globular clusters (GCs), planetary and gaseous nebulae, and nearby galaxies. This catalogue will be heavily useful for the Astronomy community.

Furthermore, using the UV catalogue of the GCs, we have studied the distribution of UV emission across the GCs and found that evolved stars, such as horizontal and post-horizontal branch stars, are the major contributors to the glimpse of UV light in GCs. We discovered a new hot post-asymptotic giant branch (PAGB) star in the Galactic GC E3, studied its detailed photometric and spectroscopic properties, and estimated various physical parameters.

We study the structure of our Galaxy using UV star counts from our proposed UVIT data in the F154W and N263M filters. The observed UVIT star counts match well with simulations from the Besan&ccedilon stellar population synthesis model in several Galactic directions. We also estimated the scale length and scale height of the thick disc and the scale height of the thin disc using the space density function and the exponential density law for the stars of intermediate Galactic latitudes.
